messages.content: 你能計算我進行的科學實驗中空氣在恆壓下的熱容量嗎？我有一個容積為2.5立方公尺的容器，並能保持溫度在300開氏度。我將在更高的溫度350開氏度重複這個實驗，接下來在更低的容積1.5立方公尺下一樣重複這個實驗。我在所有這些實驗中都使用空氣。你能提供這三種不同條件下的熱容量嗎？

function.name: calc_heat_capacity
function.description: Calculate the heat capacity at constant pressure of air using its temperature and volume. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

temp.description: The temperature of the gas in Kelvin.

volume.description: The volume of the gas in m^3. This is a float type value.

gas.description: Type of gas, with air as default.

message.content:
**Heat‑capacity at constant pressure ( \(C_{p}\) )**

For an ideal gas the molar heat capacity at constant pressure does **not** depend on the amount of substance or on the volume – it is essentially a property of the gas itself and varies very little between 200 K and 700 K for dry air.  
A good approximation for dry air in this temperature range is  

\[
c_p \;\approx\; 1005\ {\rm J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}
\]

(≈ 29 J mol\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\)).  
Because you keep the pressure fixed at one atmosphere (\(\displaystyle p\simeq 1.01325\times10^{5}\ {\rm Pa}\)), the only thing that changes from run to run is the **mass of air** contained in your vessel. Once the mass is known, the overall heat capacity follows simply from

\[
C_{\text{total}} = c_p \times m .
\]

Below I show how the masses were obtained and what the resulting heat capacities are.

---

### 1️⃣ Volume = 2.5 m³ Temperature = 300 °C (573.15 K)

| Quantity | Symbol | Value |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Gas constant for air | \(R_s\) | 287.058 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| Atmospheric pressure | \(p\) | 101 325 Pa |
| Vessel volume | \(V\) | 2.50 m³ |
| Temperature | \(T\) | 573.15 K |

**Mass of air**

\[
m=\frac{pV}{R_sT}
   =\frac{101\,325\ \mathrm{Pa}\,\times 2.50\ \mathrm{m}^{3}}
          {287.058\ \mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}\times 573.15\ \mathrm{K}}
   \approx 1.54\ \mathrm{kg}.
\]

**Total heat capacity**

\[
C_{\text{tot},1}=c_p\,m
                 =1005\ \frac{\mathrm{J}}{{\rm kg\,K}}\times 1.54\ \mathrm{kg}
                 \approx 1.55\times10^{3}\ \boxed{\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}} }.
\]

---

### 2️⃣ Same volume (2.5 m³) Higher temperature 350 °C (623.15 K)

| Quantity | Symbol | Value |
|----------|--------|-------|
| \(T\) | 623.15 K |

**Mass of air**

\[
m=\frac{pV}{R_sT}
   =\frac{101\,325\times 2.50}{287.058\times 623.15}
   \approx 1.42\ \mathrm{kg}.
\]

**Total heat capacity**

\[
C_{\text{tot},2}=1005\times 1.42
                \approx 1.43\times10^{3}\ \boxed{\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}} }.
\]

(The slight drop reflects the larger denominator \(T\); the intrinsic \(c_p\) has barely changed.)

---

### 3️⃣ Lower volume (1.5 m³) Same low temperature 300 °C (573.15 K)

| Quantity | Symbol | Value |
|----------|--------|-------|
| \(V\) | 1.50 m³ |

**Mass of air**

\[
m=\frac{pV}{R_sT}
   =\frac{101\,325\times 1.50}{287.058\times 573.15}
   \approx 0.77\ \mathrm{kg}.
\]

**Total heat capacity**

\[
C_{\text{tot},3}=1005\times 0.77
                \approx 7.74\times10^{2}\ \boxed{\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}} }.
\]

---

#### Summary table

| Run | Volume (m³) | Temp (°C) | Mass (kg) | Total \(C_p\) (J K⁻¹) |
|-----|-------------|-----------|------------|----------------------|
| 1 | 2.5 | 300 | 1.54 | 1550 |
| 2 | 2.5 | 350 | 1.42 | 1430 |
| 3 | 1.5 | 300 | 0.77 | 770  |

> **Key point:** Because \(c_p\) for dry air hardly changes over the 300–350 °C interval, all differences come from the varying amounts of air (i.e., the product \(pV/T\)).

If you want more precise numbers—especially at the upper end of the temperature scale—you might consult tabulated data for \(c_p(T)\) for air or perform a polynomial fit based on experimental measurements. However, for most laboratory purposes the above estimates should suffice.
